CFML Language Reference: Functions

REFindNoCase

Works like REFind, but letters in the expression match both upper and lower case.

Category

String functions

Syntax

REFindNoCase(reg_expression, string [, start ] [, returnsubexpressions ])

Parameters

reg_expression
The regular expression to search for. See REFind for the syntax.
string
The string to search.
start
Optional. Position at which to start searching. Default 1.
returnsubexpressions
Optional. Boolean. If true, returns a structure with pos and len arrays, as described under REFind. Default false.

Returns

The position of the first match (0 if none), or the pos/len structure.

Usage

Saves you from writing [Kk][Oo][Ll][Dd]. The POSIX classes [:upper:] and [:lower:] also match letters of either case in a case-insensitive search.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFQUERY NAME="GetParks" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT ParkName, State FROM Parks ORDER BY ParkName
</CFQUERY>
<P>Parks whose name contains "canyon" or "mesa", in any case:</P>
<UL>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="GetParks">
<CFIF REFindNoCase("canyon|mesa", ParkName)><LI>#ParkName#, #State#</CFIF>
</CFOUTPUT>
</UL>

See also

REFind, REReplaceNoCase, FindNoCase
